name: B2-W
compute_detail: Intel Core i5 (platform) + Intel Core i7 (user development); optional Intel Core i7 or Orin NX, up to 3 devices
summary: Industrial wheel-legged quadruped (B2 with wheeled feet) for long-range inspection and patrol; >40 kg walking load (120 kg standing), 15 km/h max in special configuration, ~25 km range with 40 kg.
note: Unitree B2-W page (checked 2026-11-17): standing about 1098 x 550 x 758 mm, about 85 kg with battery, wheel diameter 225 mm, battery >2 kWh at 58 V (no Wh figure), max speed 15 km/h (4.17 m/s, special configurations), 25 km with 40 kg / about 30 km unloaded, walking load >40 kg and standing load 120 kg, IP67, -20 to 55 C. No runtime in hours and no DoF are published; battery_wh and runtime_h stay empty.

name: Go2-W
compute_detail: 8-core high-performance CPU; optional expansion module (e.g. Orin NX)
summary: Consumer/education wheel-legged version of Go2 with 7-inch pneumatic in-wheel-motor tyres; runtime stated 1.5–3 h (lower bound recorded), payload ≈8 kg (max ~12 kg).
note: Unitree Go2-W page (checked 2026-11-17): 70 x 43 x 50 cm, about 18 kg, 16 joint motors, payload about 8 kg (max ~12 kg), 0-2.5 m/s, 35 deg climb, 15000 mAh battery with 1.5-3 h endurance (1.5 h recorded is the lower bound), 7-inch pneumatic tyres (178 mm).

name: A2-W
compute_detail: 8-core CPU (platform) + Intel Core i7 (user development); optional high-compute expansion dock
summary: Industrial wheel-legged quadruped for inspection, park logistics and rescue with hot-swappable dual batteries; 0–3 m/s normal, up to ~6 m/s; Pro variant adds a second LiDAR and IP56–IP67.
note: Unitree A2-W page (checked 2026-11-17): standing 900 x 440 x 625 mm, 52 kg with battery (45 kg without), tyre 190 mm diameter, 16 joint motors, single 9000 mAh (453.6 Wh) / dual (907.2 Wh) battery, 0-3 m/s up to ~6 m/s, battery life >3.5 h unloaded and >1.5 h with 25 kg, 25 kg walking load, IP56 (A2-W Pro IP56-IP67).

name: As2-W
compute_detail: 8-core high-performance CPU; optional high-compute expansion dock (e.g. Orin NX, 150 TOPS module)
summary: Compact wheel-legged quadruped with 7-inch wheels, side-follow mode and SDK/APIs for security, inspection and outdoor carrying; 0–3.7 m/s normal, ~6 m/s max.
note: Unitree As2-W page (checked 2026-11-17): 721 x 493 x 521 mm, about 25 kg with battery, 7-inch wheels (178 mm), 16 joint motors, 95 N.m peak joint torque, 648 Wh (15000 mAh) battery, 0-3.7 m/s (max ~6 m/s), about 3 h unloaded / >2 h with 16 kg, IP54, 64-128-line LiDAR, 36-50.4 V supply. The 150 TOPS figure in the summary is the optional expansion module, not standard compute.

name: LYNX M20
summary: Industrial wheel-legged quadruped for power inspection, emergency response and field work; 5 m/s lab-tested max (2 m/s operating), 80 cm single step, hot-swap batteries; M20 Pro manual lists 35 kg.
note: DEEP Robotics Lynx M20 product page (checked 2026-11-17): standing 820 x 430 x 570 mm, 33 kg with battery, payload 15 kg (maximum load 50 kg), 3 h / 15 km unloaded and 2.5 h / 12 km at 15 kg, 5 m/s lab-tested with 2 m/s safe operational speed, 25 cm continuous stair height, 80 cm single step, 45 deg slope, dual 96-line LiDAR and dual wide-angle cameras, dual octa-core processors, IP66, -20 to 55 C, 72 V input, 1.5 h single-battery charge. DoF (16) comes from the M20 Pro user manual, not the product page; battery capacity is not published.

name: TRON 1
price_note: Standard Edition on LimX online shop (EDU Ed. $25,000)
summary: Multi-modal biped research robot with swappable point-foot, sole and wheeled feet for RL and embodied-AI research; ≤3 m/s in wheeled mode, open SDK with Isaac/MuJoCo/Gazebo support.
note: LimX TRON 1 spec page (checked 2026-11-17): dimensions <=392 x 420 x 845 mm, net weight <=20 kg, payload 10 kg, speed 1 m/s point-foot / 1 m/s sole / 3 m/s wheeled, 30 deg climb, 20 cm obstacle, 2 h battery life, 4.5 Ah at 46.8 V (about 210.6 Wh, derived - the maker gives no Wh figure), 12th-gen Intel i3 / 16 GB / 512 GB computer, -5 to 40 C, RGBD camera optional, IMU standard. Degrees of freedom are not stated.

name: DIABLO
summary: Self-balancing two-wheel-legged open development platform with six direct-drive joints; 4 kg payload standing, 80 kg in crouched mode, near-silent operation.
note: Direct Drive Technology Diablo product page (checked 2026-11-17): standing 540 x 371 x 491 mm (crouched 540 x 371 x 270 mm), 22.9 kg incl. docking mechanism, 6 DoF, battery 0.178 kWh (178 Wh), runtime about 1.5 h, charge about 1 h, payload 4 kg standing / 80 kg crouched, 2 m/s, 80 mm jump, Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, Ubuntu 20.04.

name: Ascento Guard
price_note: Robotics-as-a-Service (hired by the hour); no list price
summary: Two-wheeled, legged self-balancing autonomous outdoor security patrol robot sold as RaaS, with autonomous charging and 8 h+ battery (2023 launch spec: <30 kg, 4.5 h).
note: Ascento's own site (checked 2026-11-17) states 8 h battery life with fast charging and 24/7 availability for Guard, sold only as Robotics-as-a-Service. The maker's September 2023 launch factsheet, as reported at launch, gave 4.5 h and a walking speed of about 1.4 m/s with a system weight under 30 kg; those figures are press-sourced and the runtime conflict is recorded here rather than resolved. Ascento publishes no product page with a full specification table, so mass, dimensions and speed stay empty.

name: RIVR ONE
summary: Wheeled-legged doorstep-delivery robot (formerly Swiss-Mile) that rides sidewalks at up to 14 km/h and climbs stairs; carries >30 kg, >30 km range, can deploy from delivery vans.
note: RIVR's product page (checked 2026-11-17): wheeled-legged doorstep delivery robot that rides sidewalks and bike lanes, climbs stairs and opens gates; more than 30 kg payload, up to 14 km/h (3.89 m/s) when needed, over 30 km range with a 2-3 h recharge, and van-dispensed delivery mode. Mass, dimensions and battery capacity are not published.

name: MobED Pro
summary: Production autonomous mobility platform using eccentric Drive-and-Lift wheel modules for posture control over curbs (100–200 mm) and slopes; Ethernet API, follow-me; unveiled iREX Dec 2025 with sales scheduled H1 2026.
note: Hyundai Motor Group press release at iREX 2025 (3 Dec 2025) specification table: Pro up to 750 x 1150 x 650 mm incl. antenna, tare weight up to 88 kg, maximum payload up to 47 kg, autonomous (Autonomous/Smart Assist) plus manual modes, up to 0.3 m/s in inward posture and up to 2.8 m/s otherwise, 1.47 kWh at 36-49.2 V, >=4 h, charge <=2 h 30 min, IP54, 0-40 C, Ethernet API. Sensor set from the HMG Journal piece: GPS, two 3D LiDARs, three cameras, eight radars and an IMU.

name: MobED Basic
summary: R&D version of MobED without pre-installed autonomy (manual drive, RS422 API) built on the eccentric Drive-and-Lift wheel modules; sales scheduled H1 2026.
note: Hyundai Motor Group press release at iREX 2025 (3 Dec 2025) specification table: Basic up to 750 x 1150 x 430 mm, tare weight up to 78 kg, maximum payload up to 57 kg, manual drive only (Basic/Freestyle/Zigzag, no autonomous mode), up to 2.8 m/s outside the inward posture, battery rated capacity 1.47 kWh at 36-49.2 V, operating time >=4 h (BMS 90->10 %), charge <=2 h 30 min, IP54, 0-40 C, RS422 API, no pre-installed autonomy. No degrees of freedom are published.

name: Lynx S10
compute_detail: Octa-core 64-bit industrial processor (×1 S10, ×2 S10 Pro)
summary: Compact 21 kg all-terrain wheel-legged robot for inspection, patrol, search-and-rescue and research, IP66-rated with autonomous charging.
note: max_speed_mps uses the stated max operating speed (2 m/s); the page also cites a 6.8 m/s 'max tested speed' under extreme lab conditions. Sensors per S10 Pro column (S10 base: 1 LiDAR, 1 camera).

name: MagicDog-W
summary: Wheeled quadruped combining legs with pneumatic wheels for research, demos, patrol and surveying; 10 kg payload, 3 m/s.
note: Speed stated '≥3.0 m/s'; runtime 2–4 h (lower bound used). 7-inch pneumatic tires (177.8 mm). Dimensions standing L×W×H.

name: D5-W
compute_detail: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64GB + RK3588 (up to 275 TOPS)
summary: Wheeled-leg variant of PUDU D5 for fast all-terrain delivery and inspection, IP67, up to 5 m/s.
note: Same page as D5 (D5-W column). Payload 20–30 kg (lower bound); runtime 2–3 h.

name: RIVR TWO
summary: Second-generation wheeled-legged robot that delivers parcels and food autonomously to the doorstep, climbing curbs and steps.
note: RIVR (RIVR Technologies AG, Zurich) page confirms RIVR TWO, a wheeled-legged doorstep-delivery robot with top-load/bottom-release 55 L payload bay (volume only, payload_kg left out). Amazon acquired RIVR in March 2026 (press). Speed 14 km/h and >60 lb payload appear only on RIVR ONE/product page or press, not on RIVR TWO page - left out. Status set to Pilot: RIVR's partner deployments (e.g. Evri, 2025) were RIVR ONE; no general-availability statement for RIVR TWO seen.

name: W1
summary: Wheel-legged quadruped from LimX Dynamics that rolls, steps and climbs stairs and can stand up to move on two wheeled legs, aimed at inspection, logistics and research.
note: Confirmed by LimX press releases: launched 25 Sep 2023 as a wheeled quadruped (pre-orders from Q4 2023); May 2024 update added a biped (stand-up) mode. Heights per maker: prone 350 mm, quadruped mode 550 mm (height_mm), biped mode 1520 mm. W1 is no longer on LimX's current product list (Luna, Oli, TRON 1, TRON 2) -> status set Discontinued (inferred from removal, no maker EOL notice seen). Aggregator figures (5.98 m/s / 10 m/s speed, 864 Wh battery, 16 DoF, 50 kg payload, 240 min runtime, 5 stereo cameras) are NOT maker-confirmed on pages opened - not filled.

name: RHP Bex
summary: Kawasaki's goat-like wheel-legged quadruped prototype that walks on rough ground or rolls on knee wheels, targeting 100 kg cargo, inspection and farm transport.
note: Kawasaki's own blog (interview, 2023) confirms RHP Bex as a four-legged Kaleido derivative first shown at iREX 2022 (March 2022), with knee wheels for rolling on flat ground (wheel-legged). Payload is a development TARGET of 100 kg (stated as target, filled as payload_kg with this caveat); demonstrated carrying a rider. Upper body modular (offered as open platform for partners). Still under development - status Research; no dims, weight, speed or price published. Kawasaki's separate CORLEO rideable quadruped (2025) is a different product.

name: Max
summary: Tencent Robotics X research quadruped with wheels on its knees, switching between walking and rolling at up to 25 km/h.
note: Tencent official WeChat announcement (2021-03-02) and Tencent news account (gen-2 Max, 2022-08-08); research platform, not sold. Wheels on knees.

name: FX Aegis Mega
summary: Mid-size IP67 wheel-legged industrial robot dog with dual 96-line LiDAR, from $74,990 (Mega A / Mega D).
note: 8 m/s is Mega A lab top speed (Mega D 5 m/s; recommended working speed 2 m/s). Dimensions/weight/payload converted from shop's 36.6x18.9x23 in, 90 lb, 55 lb rated; Forbes' 50 kg payload doesn't match the maker. 16 DOF = 12 joints + 4 hub motors.

name: Qiji XS
summary: Rideable 320 kg wheel-legged robot horse that cruises on wheels at over 40 km/h and switches to legs for rough terrain.
note: Scope review (#16, 2026-11-17): kept as an in-scope Wheel-legged - a wheel-foot robot horse that drives on wheels on flat ground and switches to legs for rough terrain; rideable is not an excluded category here (see CORLEO, RHP Bex). DaxAI's own releases conflict on range: 100 km (WAIC, July 2026) vs 60 km (WRC, Aug 2026), and press repeats 60 km. Not yet shown running in public per press. No XS page on the maker's site (daxrobotics.cn lists 骑骥 T1000 only).

name: DEEP Robotics Lynx (first generation)
summary: DEEP Robotics' original 30 kg wheel-legged all-terrain robot that climbs 80 cm platforms and reaches 5 m/s.
note: First generation of the LYNX wheel-legged line. Superseded in DEEP's lineup by the LYNX M20 (industrial, 2025) and Lynx S10 (2026) -> Discontinued: the maker's product list marks the earlier LYNX Sport line as discontinued and offers M20/S10 in its place, and this record's gen-1 page (deeprobotics.cn/en/index/deeproboticslynx.html) now returns 404 (checked 2026-11-17). Range 15 km, step height 22 cm.

name: C1-W
compute_detail: x86 or domestic low-power ARM CPU
summary: Small industrial wheel-legged robot (19 kg, IP67) for inspection, climbing 70 cm steps, with 8 kg payload and up to 5 h runtime.
note: Specs from Galileo (Tianjin) official product brochure (maker PDF hosted on WRC exhibitor site); product also listed on official site galileotimes.com. max_speed is stated limit (极限) speed; runtime range 2.5–5 h, upper value used; max payload 15 kg. Re-checked 2026-11-17: maker's own product page opened (galileotimes.com, Galileo Tianjin's product site, contacts @galileotime.com). Its current parameter table for this model reads - C1-W (wheel-legged) column: 765x480x540 mm, 28.5 kg, 20Ah/960 Wh 48 V, 0-5 m/s, >=30 deg slope, >=20 cm steps, 3-5 h, 12 kg continuous load, IP67. The stored numbers come from Galileo's 2025 product manual (maker PDF) and are LOWER/lighter than the current page (C1 660x320x470 mm /15 kg vs 765x410x475 mm /22 kg; E1 1000x420x600 mm /38 kg vs 1000x452x550 mm /52 kg; S1 1100x450x700 mm /60 kg vs 1200x550x650 mm /118 kg), i.e. the page appears to describe the 2026 line-up. Stored values kept so this PR does not silently rewrite specs; the current-page figures are recorded here for the owner to choose between.

name: Genisom L1-W
compute_detail: 8-core CPU (EDU: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, 100 TOPS)
summary: 22 kg wheel-legged robot dog with 12 joints plus 4 hub motors, 5.5 m/s limit speed, 65 cm obstacle crossing, IP54.
note: GENISOM AI official page 钢镚 L1-W: 12 joint motors + 4 hub motors; limit speed 5.5 m/s; payload ≈10 kg (limit ~12 kg).

name: Genisom L2-W
summary: 27 kg wheel-legged variant of the Gangben L2 quadruped: IP66, 16 kg payload, up to 5.5 h runtime, LiDAR+GNSS navigation.
note: Official URL is the 钢镚 L2 page, whose spec table lists L2 (point-foot), L2-W (wheel-legged) and L2-W Ultra; values here are L2-W. Limit speed 5 m/s; payload ≈16 kg (150 kg static). '¥39,999 起' on page is the L2 family starting price, not specific to L2-W, so price left null. 756 Wh battery stated on page (spec table lists 15000 mAh). Re-checked 2026-11-17: the L2 product page (opened) carries a per-variant spec table with an explicit L2-W column - standing 760x450x500 mm, prone 780x550x190 mm, 27 kg with battery, ~16 kg continuous payload (150 kg static), 3.7 m/s max / 5 m/s limit, 25 cm continuous stairs, 40 deg slope, 5.5 h no-load / 3.5 h full-load, 20 km / 12 km range, 756 Wh (15000 mAh), 1.5 h charge, 12 joint motors / 95 N.m, 4G, UWB, stereo camera, IP66, -20~55 C. CORRECTION: LiDAR and GNSS/RTK are NOT in the L2-W column (the 96-line LiDAR x2 and RTK are L2-W Ultra only), so they were removed from sensors; dof filled with the 12 joint motors. The page's marketing copy ('RoamerX ... LiDAR + GNSS', '720 deg fusion sensing') describes the family, not the L2-W configuration.

name: TIGER X-1
summary: Uncrewed transforming Ultimate Mobility Vehicle concept (TIGER X-1) with four leg-and-wheel units that drives on retracted legs and walks over terrain that stops a wheeled vehicle, built around an internal cargo bay.
note: Hyundai Motor Group's TIGER press release (Feb 2021, hyundai.com) describes TIGER X-1 as the experimental first version developed by New Horizons Studio with Autodesk and Sundberg-Ferar: four leg-and-wheel units, 360-degree directional control, an internal load bay and sensors for remote observation. The maker publishes no mass, dimensions, speed, payload or battery figure for X-1, so no spec field is filled.

name: Four-Wheeled Robot
summary: Sheet-metal industrial quadruped from SVT Robot (时空变量) for teleoperation, imitation learning and data collection, military reconnaissance and search and rescue.
note: SVT Robot product page (checked 2026-11-17): 820 x 430 x 570 mm, 33 kg with battery, effective payload 20-30 kg (20 kg recorded as the lower bound), 3 h / 15 km unloaded and 2.5 h / 12 km loaded, 5 m/s limit and 2 m/s working speed, 25 cm stair height, 80 cm step, 45 degree slope, dual 96-line LiDAR and wide-angle camera, dual battery pack with BMS, octa-core industrial controller, CAN/RS485/USB, 1.5 h charge per battery. The maker gives no battery capacity, DoF or IP rating.

name: Y20-W
summary: Wheel-legged version of the Yobotics Y20 announced on 18 September 2025 for all-terrain inspection work.
note: Yobotics announced Y20-W on 18 September 2025 and lists it in the quadruped catalogue, but its parameter table is published only as a graphic on the maker's site; no text specification, datasheet or PDF was found, so no field is filled from the maker and the record stays unconfirmed. Third-party transcriptions of that graphic (e.g. 920 x 550 x 670 mm, 52 kg, IP67, 40 kg dynamic load) are not maker sources and were not used.

name: YJ30 W
note: Yuejia Lingdong YJ30W page and brochure (checked 2026-11-17): standing 682 x 354 x 532 mm, 20 kg, payload 12 kg, 1.5-2 h (3.5-4 h with a second battery), 60 cm stair, 5 m/s, 50 deg climb, IP54. DoF is merged with climb angle in the maker table and not stated separately.
